reason: Fit the load tray to the test stand so there is somewhere to place and balance the test load.
expectation: The tray will attach to the tethered lift setup, ready for a balance test.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the crane sling may help lift a load, but I would start by fitting the tray.

effect: The tray is fitted, so I can now test how an off-centre load affects balance.
reaction: A straightforward preparation; nothing surprising yet.
reason: Add the off-centre block to reveal how the loaded tile behaves before balancing it.
expectation: The load will make the tray tilt or otherwise show an imbalance, while the tether keeps the test contained.

alternatives.reason: The crane sling may be useful later, but the block advances the balance test now.

effect: The loaded end dips, confirming that lift alone does not balance the tray. I should try the counterweight.
reaction: The tilt makes the balance problem clear.
reason: Use the sliding counterweight to counter the off-centre load.
expectation: Moving the counterweight should bring the tray closer to level, though it may need adjustment.

alternatives.reason: The crane sling could be useful later, but it does not address the visible tilt.

effect: The counterweight leveled the tray but increased the load, so it needs more lift.
reaction: The trade-off between balance and added weight is clear and interesting.
reason: Fit the current controller to adjust the lift for the heavier tray.
expectation: The controller should let me increase lift enough for the balanced load, though it may still need a separate stop.

alternatives.reason: The crane sling may be useful later, but the controller addresses the extra load now.

effect: The lift module now has adjustable power; it still needs a reliable stop.
reaction: A straightforward fitting, with no detail yet about how the adjustment works.
reason: Fit the power-cut switch to address the goal of a reliable stop.
expectation: The switch should cut power and stay off until reset, though I don't yet know how it will be tested.

alternatives.reason: The crane sling may be useful later, but the switch directly addresses the remaining goal.

effect: The power-cut switch overrides the controller, demonstrating a stop during the tethered test.
reaction: The override makes the stop's purpose clear.
reason: Prepare the crane with the sling; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: The sling will attach to the crane, probably to move the lift module, though its exact use is not yet clear.

effect: The sling is attached to the crane, ready to handle the stopped lift module.
reaction: A straightforward preparation; its exact purpose is still unclear.
reason: Use the sling-equipped crane on the module; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: The crane will lift or support the stopped module, perhaps to remove it from the stand.

effect: The crane now supports the lift module in its sling, ready for release.
reaction: The sling's purpose is clearer now.
reason: Use the release spanner on the supported module; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect the spanner to release the module from the test stand while the crane supports it.

effect: The crane supported the module while it was released, completing the balanced lift module with its tether and controls intact.
reaction: The supported release neatly explained why the crane and sling were needed.

mostWorthwhile.text: Balancing the tilting tray was the strongest moment: the counterweight corrected the tilt but added load, making the trade-off easy to understand.

leastWorthwhile.text: Preparing the crane and sling was straightforward, but its purpose was initially unclear and the separate fittings felt a little drawn out.

surprise.text: The counterweight made the tray level but meant it needed more lift; correcting one problem introduced another.

arbitrary.text: The sling preparation initially lacked a clear purpose, though supporting the module for release explained it afterward.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the balanced module is used in the flying fair; the balance and safety tests gave that next construction a clear setup.
